obligation: Tier 1 public notice
trigger: Waterborne emergency, such as a failure or significant interruption in key water treatment processes (for example unsafe hypochlorite feed or loss of disinfection reaching distribution), or another situation the primacy agency designates Tier 1
deadline: As soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the violation or situation
notify: All persons served by the affected system, by broadcast media, posting, hand delivery, or another method approved in writing by the primacy agency; Spanish statement where required (141.205(c)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, all 11 systems, if key treatment was interrupted or off-spec water may have entered distribution. Runbook 1 D1; runbook 2 D6
clock_starts: When the system learns of the violation or situation (incident log, POL-03 statement 4.3)
owner: Water Quality and Compliance Manager with the Chief Operating Officer

obligation: Primacy agency consultation
trigger: Same as the Tier 1 notice
deadline: Initiate as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after learning of the situation; then follow any added requirements from the consultation
notify: State drinking water primacy agency (after-hours line in the public notice SOP)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes with any Tier 1 situation. Company rule: courtesy call for any confirmed tampering even without a Tier 1 trigger

obligation: Notice to the consecutive system (wholesale city)
trigger: A violation or situation requiring public notice in water the Regional System sells to the neighboring city
deadline: Same tier and timing as the notice to the company's own customers
notify: Owner or operator of the consecutive system, which then notifies its own customers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the Regional System only

obligation: Copy of the notice and certification to the primacy agency
trigger: Completion of the initial public notice and any repeat notices
deadline: Within 10 days of completing the public notification requirements, with a representative copy of each type of notice
notify: State drinking water primacy agency
applies_at_this_tier: Yes after any public notice

obligation: Report failure to comply with a drinking water regulation
trigger: The incident causes a violation of a national primary drinking water regulation, including missed required monitoring
deadline: Within 48 hours (unless the part sets a different period)
notify: State drinking water primacy agency
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a violation results (for example missed compliance monitoring while SCADA is down)

obligation: Ground Water Rule: grab sampling when continuous monitoring fails
trigger: Failure of continuous residual disinfectant monitoring at a system serving more than 3,300 people (for example analyzers or SCADA unavailable during an incident)
deadline: Grab samples every 4 hours until continuous monitoring is back in service; resume continuous monitoring within 14 days
notify: Internal (laboratory and operations records); failures feed the next two rows
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the Regional, Lakes, and Ridge Systems. Small systems take a daily grab sample under 141.403(b)(3)(i)(B)
clock_starts: Failure of the continuous monitoring equipment

obligation: Ground Water Rule: residual below the state minimum
trigger: The system fails to meet the state-specified minimum residual disinfectant concentration and does not restore it within 4 hours
deadline: As soon as possible, but no later than the end of the next business day
notify: State drinking water primacy agency
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, all 11 systems (all conduct compliance monitoring under 141.403(b))

obligation: Retain public notices and certifications
trigger: Any public notice issued
deadline: Keep copies for 3 years after issuance
notify: Internal record (compliance file)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes after any public notice

obligation: Law enforcement referral for tampering
citation: 42 U.S.C. 300i-1 (tampering, attempt, or threat to tamper with a public water system is a federal crime)
trigger: Evidence that someone interfered or attempted to interfere with the operation of a water system
deadline: No statutory reporting deadline. Company rule: notify the FBI as soon as the incident is declared (POL-03 statement 4.7)
notify: FBI field office (and IC3 online report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for any confirmed unauthorized control action. Preserve evidence for investigators

obligation: Voluntary cyber incident report
citation: Voluntary. No federal mandatory cyber incident reporting rule applied to water systems as of 2026-10-05
trigger: Any significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as possible. Company rule: within 24 hours of declaration
notify: CISA and the water-sector ISAC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary). Reporting to law enforcement or CISA is also a mitigating factor for OFAC if a ransom is ever considered

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-05. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered on two grounds: it exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 221310, and it owns community water systems serving more than 3,300 people. Recheck when final

obligation: ERP and RRA update after an incident
trigger: A significant incident that shows the RRA or ERP no longer reflects the system
deadline: No statutory deadline for an incident-driven update. Company rule: review within 60 days of recovery (POL-03 statement 4.13)
notify: Internal; EPA certification only at the next required review or revision
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the Regional, Lakes, and Ridge Systems

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example customer names with online account credentials, or with bank account details plus the code needed to access the account)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; a 15-day extension is available for this notice only, with good cause given in writing to the Department within the 30 days; law enforcement may delay it by written request
notify: Affected Florida residents (mail or email; substitute notice if allowed)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information was accessed. An HMI compromise alone does not trigger it
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (decision log)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Floridians are affected

obligation: Florida no-notice determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep at least 5 years, and provide to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the company decides not to notify individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals are notified at once (likely in any CIS breach)

obligation: Third-party agent notice to municipal clients (outbound)
trigger: Breach of client customers' personal information held by the company in the CIS as the clients' third-party agent
deadline: Statute: no later than 10 days after the company's determination. Contract: within 24 hours of a security incident affecting client data
notify: Each affected municipal client (which then gives the notices required of it)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for 15,600 client accounts. Agree with each client who sends notices to its customers
owner: Director of Utility Services with the General Counsel

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains or processes customer personal information for the company (CIS, AMI, print-and-mail, notification vendor) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The company (Director of Customer Service and the Security Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts; 2 of 5 contracts lack a term (P03 G-070)

obligation: Other states' breach notification
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of another state (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if affected customers have out-of-state billing addresses (about 6% of customers). Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Utility Services contract notice to clients (monitoring)
trigger: Any security incident affecting a client's plant monitoring at the ROC, or alarm acknowledgment beyond 15 minutes
deadline: Within 24 hours of the incident
notify: Each affected municipal client
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Payment processor notice
trigger: Possible tampering with the customer portal link to the processor's hosted payment page, or with the IVR transfer to the processor's phone line
deadline: Per the agreement (as soon as practicable)
notify: Payment processor
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the portal or IVR could have redirected payments; card numbers never enter company systems

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (as soon as practicable; call the carrier hotline before hiring outside vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Board and PE sponsor notice
trigger: Any severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 48 hours of declaration
notify: Audit committee chair; PE sponsor's operating partner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company rule
